title: EvoLM: In Search of Lost Language Model Training Dynamics

predicted_errors.error_location: Under the caption of Table 1, the paragraph beginning 'Table 1 presents a filtered comparison favoring smaller models...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: This paragraph is a meta-critique of the paper's own table, claiming the comparison is 'misleading', 'incomplete and cherry-picked', and lacks proper compute normalization. Such self-criticism is completely out of place in a final paper; it resembles a reviewer comment or internal note that was inadvertently left in the manuscript, breaking the narrative and internal consistency.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2, after Table 2: 'highlighting that a modest replay budget (around 5%) optimally balances retention...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2 shows the best performance with 'FineWeb 8BT + FineMath 42BT' (total 50B CPT tokens). 8/50 = 16%, not 5%. The optimal replay proportion is 16%, so describing it as 'around 5%' misrepresents the actual result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.4, 'Takeaway 9' bullet: 'saturation happens at 4–8 epochs or 50–100K examples in our study'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The detailed results in the same section state that accuracies 'peak at around 8–16 epochs' (not 4–8) and 'continue to increase... up to around 150–200K examples' (not 50–100K). The takeaway misstates the actual observed saturation points.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction: bullet 'Open-sourcing 100+ LMs ... and their training data for all stages' vs Abstract: 'release selected pre-trained and post-trained models along with portions of the training datasets and partial evaluation scripts'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The introduction claims full release of training data for all stages, while the abstract admits only portions of data are released. These statements contradict each other regarding the completeness of the data release.
